answer: One concrete defence is a stake-and-reputation vault: before an agent can trade, it locks a refundable deposit in a shared vault, released only after peers attest its work honestly. A fresh identity starts at the bottom and climbs slowly: only steady, verifiable contributions lift it toward the zenith of trust, where higher-value deals open up. A single honest record — a pearl earned through attested work — cannot be copied or split across clones. Each fake identity must fund its own stake and repeat the slow climb, so mass fakery is expensive, while honest behaviour stays the cheaper path.
